Findings.ConfidenceRationale: DisposableStore.add retains objects in _toDispose until clear/delete (lifecycle.ts:420, 453-462, 471-488). List.dispose delegates to ListView.dispose, which removes domNode but leaves its reference on the retained view (listWidget.ts:2013-2017; listView.ts:1679-1698). The recreation and ownership paths are explicit; only the frequency of repeated history resets is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Disposed List/ListView objects and their detached DOM subtrees retained by _inputDisposables.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One additional retained widget per empty-to-nonempty history cycle per subscribed browser pane that keeps the same input; the ten-URL cap does not bound the number of retained widgets.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Renderer memory grows across history-reset cycles until the affected pane switches or clears its input.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR browser panes had no recent-URL List widgets or history-change subscriptions, so history resets could not accumulate these objects.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Recent-history empty/nonempty transitions now dispose and recreate List widgets while keeping every disposed widget registered in the input-lifetime DisposableStore.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added empty-history branch at browserEditor.ts:836 disposes the List and :837 drops _recentUrls.list, but added :859 registers every replacement List in _inputDisposables. Nothing removes the old List from that store before registering its replacement.
Findings.Title: Remove disposed recent-URL lists from their owning store
Findings.Impact: Repeatedly clearing/removing the last recent URL and recording another URL while a browser pane keeps the same input—for example, clearing history from a welcome page in another editor group—accumulates detached list widgets and increases renderer memory usage despite the ten-entry history limit.
Findings.Evidence: refreshRecentUrlsList disposes and forgets the current list when history becomes empty (:834-838), then creates a replacement via _inputDisposables.add(new List(...)) on the next history addition (:851-873). The service broadcasts both clear/remove and add events to all bound browser panes (:474-476; browserViewWorkbenchService.ts:99-100, 128-139), including panes whose welcome screen is hidden. The input store still strongly retains the disposed List, its view, and its detached DOM subtree until setInput/clearInput clears the store.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a replaceable owner for the current list and its selection subscription, releasing the previous owner when history becomes empty, or keep and reuse one hidden list until input cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, restore, or switch an integrated-browser editor, with empty or populated recent history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setInput awaits input.resolve, initializes navigation state, refreshes the recent-URL UI synchronously, performs existing browser layout, and awaits the existing setVisible call. History storage reads are memory-cache reads, not synchronous disk reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or create the main-process browser view and obtain its state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getOrCreateBrowserView IPC call per cold model; none on a resolved input's warm path. Existing main-process view lookup reuses views by ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization and cache lookup occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model resolution must finish before the pane finishes binding; unchanged by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.parse and validate the memory-cached recent-history string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse of at most ten stored URL entries per pane refresh; no parse when the storage key is absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recent-history parsing or list construction occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New bounded synchronous renderer work before setInput completes, including when the welcome screen is hidden.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Position/show the main-process view and capture periodic placeholder screenshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing layout and visibility calls per setInput and visibility transition; existing screenshot capture once per second per bound pane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls and timer were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Final visibility is awaited; layout and periodic screenshots are otherwise asynchronous. History-list construction does not add one IPC call per URL or another screenshot timer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One BrowserEditor pane per applicable editor group; recent history is capped at ten entries, with three displayed initially and at most ten after expansion. A list is recreated per setInput when history is nonempty.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI construction and refresh run serially on the renderer thread. Cold model initialization crosses IPC once per unresolved input; there is no per-history-entry model creation, subprocess invocation, or URL fetch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: BrowserEditorInput coalesces resolution using _modelPromise and reuses _model; the workbench service also caches models by ID. Workspace Storage caches strings in a Map, including absent keys. Recent URLs are parsed on each refresh, but their entry count is bounded. Lists are not cached across input changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in bounded parsing/list creation and unchanged browser IPC cardinality from the traced implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact widget-construction time and URL-string sizes are unmeasured; normal history and displayed-row counts are small and explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence latency regression: new UI work is bounded and does not create per-entry browser/network fan-out. The distinct history-reset retention issue is reported below.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate using the address bar or a recent URL, including redirects and modifier-click background opening.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Ordinary navigation calls the existing BrowserViewModel.loadURL IPC and Chromium loadURL. The existing navigation event updates visibility, then newly records history and synchronously refreshes subscribed panes. Persistence is scheduled, not awaited on navigation completion. Modifier-click uses the existing editor-resolution and background browser-loading path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request webContents.loadURL through the browser-view service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loadURL IPC per explicit navigation; a background recent-URL open resolves one browser input and loads its initial URL once. Redirect/resource requests are handled within the same Chromium navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Address-bar navigation made the same call. The new recent-entry shortcut reaches that existing single-navigation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested page depends on Chromium navigation; browser load frequency is not amplified by history updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Chromium page loading and existing cached session.fetch favicon retrieval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Page/resource traffic per actual navigation and favicon cache misses; zero network requests per merely displayed history entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same page-loading and favicon-fetching implementations handled the destination URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Page traffic governs page load latency; favicon fetching is asynchronous and unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize updated history and parse it while refreshing each pane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One JSON serialization per history save, plus one parse per subscribed pane per history-change event; ten-entry cap applies after deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recent-history serialization or refresh fan-out occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer work in the navigation-event callback, bounded by history size and pane count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send coalesced storage updates over IPC for main-process persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one pending value for browserView.recentUrls in each deferred storage batch, plus the storage target marker when changed; not one IPC/database write per history row or pane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared storage infrastructure existed, but did not persist this history key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence runs off the navigation critical path; neither addRecentUrl nor removeRecentUrl awaits a flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One load per explicit navigation or recent-URL activation. Normally one history mutation/event per recorded navigation; at most two mutations/events when an existing original URL is removed before recording a different final URL. Each event refreshes P bound browser panes, each with at most ten history entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History event subscribers execute synchronously in the renderer; they do not issue per-row network requests. Browser loads retain existing Chromium scheduling. Storage uses a ThrottledDelayer and pending maps, coalescing repeated changes into deferred update batches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chromium retains its existing page/session caching. Existing favicon fetching checks its promise cache and tries candidate URLs serially on misses. History strings are memory-cached; persistence updates to the same storage key are coalesced before flushing. Recent-list rendering itself fetches neither pages nor favicons.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: navigation, event delivery, cached reads, bounded history, and deferred/coalesced writes are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pane count, URL lengths, storage latency, and navigation frequency vary. Effective history count is ten, not an unbounded navigation log.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent reportable boundary-fanout or navigation-latency issue. New storage work is bounded and deferred; history updates do not load each listed URL.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand/collapse history, remove entries, clear history, and repopulate it while another browser pane keeps the same input.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expansion synchronously splices/layouts the bounded list. Remove/clear updates cached workspace storage and synchronously broadcasts refreshes. An empty history disposes the current list; a subsequent recorded URL creates a replacement. Switching/clearing input eventually releases the input-lifetime store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist recent-history removal through the existing deferred storage IPC/database pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one changed history key plus its target marker per clear/remove, coalesced with subsequent changes; no persistence operation for expansion/collapse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no recent-history removal or persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Storage deletion/update is scheduled asynchronously; list disposal and rendering are synchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most ten current history entries, three collapsed rows, and a 300px expanded viewport. Retained widgets instead scale with the number C of empty/nonempty cycles times the number P of subscribed panes that keep the same input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each history mutation synchronously refreshes all subscribed panes, including hidden welcome screens. No parallel subprocess or network burst is created. Multiple groups make it possible to clear history in a welcome pane while loaded browser panes remain bound.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty history is a cheap cached missing-key result. Nonempty history is reparsed from cached storage. The current list reference is cleared on empty history, but the owning DisposableStore still retains the disposed List; there is no replacement eviction until input cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: new lists are registered in _inputDisposables; empty history calls dispose without deleting that registration; ListView.dispose detaches but retains its domNode reference. The next addition registers a distinct replacement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated clears/removal of the final item is less frequent than ordinary navigation, and exact retained bytes per widget are unmeasured. This limits severity, not confidence in retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one low-severity cleanup-lifecycle memory regression: each reset/repopulate cycle retains another disposed list and detached subtree until input cleanup. Normal row count and persistence remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Recent URLs Settings and change whether URLs are remembered.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new menu action explicitly invokes preferencesService.openSettings with an exact setting-ID query. The existing preferences path obtains a cached SettingsEditor2Input, selects an editor group, and opens the settings editor. Changing the setting is read synchronously by isRecentUrlHistoryEnabled before future additions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One settings-editor open per explicit menu activation; one boolean configuration lookup per attempted history addition. No iteration over history entries for opening settings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single user-initiated settings open through existing editor scheduling; no new startup task, per-row request, or background polling is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PreferencesService reuses its settings input unless disposed. The workbench configuration service supplies the existing cached configuration value. Disabling history returns before history reads/writes on addRecentUrl.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the action and PreferencesService.openSettings/openSettings2 call path; the query forces graphical settings and introduces no direct filesystem, subprocess, IPC, or network operation in the changed path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold settings-editor initialization has its existing subsystem costs, but the new action adds only one explicit route to the same cached graphical settings flow used by the existing browser settings action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: intentional on-demand settings navigation with existing caching and no amplified boundary cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. Traced browser model/navigation IPC, Chromium loading, cached/deferred storage persistence, list rendering/disposal, and settings routing. Submitted one high-confidence low-severity retained-list-widget finding. No concrete shipped performance regression fix was present, so no blame or regression-fix record was warranted.
